reply_text:
I've finished the polish notes. Next I'm reading the McCarthy requirements file so my comments on the strategy are grounded.㊥ I've done the polish notes, and on the strategy I'd start with the small "proposal: accepted, declined, or no response" model, before either the McCarthy requirements or the Fong upgrade. First, though, one question decides what "no response" means: should a proposal Joe never answered count as declined after his next turn, or only after a fixed number of turns?

🈰 (implement their polish notes) All are done; none of it is on the live site.

| Review point | Fix | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1, 2 | "causal theory together with a model"; "in the spirit of [3]" | futon3c `a64bcee5` |
| 3 | the text now says `asked` is set by hand in `observe` | `a64bcee5` |
| 4 | real bug fixed: a problem answered by three or more patterns silently lost all but two, because the equation parser only takes a two-input `or`; `link-theory` now chains them | `a64bcee5` |
| 5 | notes 象 was switched back on at 22:55 the same day | `a64bcee5` |
| 6 | McCarthy citation: I checked the Stanford page. It is dated 6 Nov 1998 and nothing on it supports "1992", so the reference now says 1998 and gives the URL | `eea89bf0` |
| 7, 8 | 小象 lead-in moved back above the box; "reads our own agents' conversations after every turn" | staging `63392e6`, pushed |

The notebook is republished. Its computed values are unchanged: the WR-26 cone has no problem answered by more than two patterns. The tangle test passes (2 tests, 6 assertions).

🈯 (their strategy) The strategy has three parts:
1. on the McCarthy side, restore R3, R12 and R19;
2. on the Fong side, move to typed ports and finite kernels;
3. where they meet, build a small model for "proposal → accepted / declined / no response".

My view on each:

㊣ (where the two join) Start with part 3. Three things need it: the reminder machine, the ask arm in M-zaif-harness, and WR-0's 108 unanswered proposals. The data mostly exists already:
- an agent's ㊭ paragraph is a proposal;
- your `㊣:` or `🈚:` reply, in the colon form, names the proposal it answers;
- so most of the table can be counted from logs we already keep.

The hard cell is telling a proposal you saw and declined from one you never saw. Text alone can't separate them, but there is one observable we already know about: voxterm speaks only the first paragraph. A ㊭ in paragraph three may never have reached you. So "was it in the gist?" should go into the model, alongside whether you took a turn afterwards.

㊭ (McCarthy side, order) I'd do R19 next. It's mostly done already:
- the kernel already computes "created and not cancelled";
- what's missing is an act that cancels, and DERIVE-1 says "revoke has no act type";
- the proforma now has 🈡 withdraw and 🈹 retract, so 大象 could turn those into cancel acts.

R12 (joint acts) mostly falls out of the colon form: agent ㊭ followed by your `㊣:` is an agreement. R3 (generating correctness conditions) is the biggest of the three. The cascade compiler's `k-unmet` rule is a small generator of that kind already, so R3 can grow from it rather than starting fresh.

㊟ (Fong side) I'd hold off building typed ports and kernels until the research report answers Q1, because we don't yet know which construction `ot/glue` is. Two things argue for the kernels eventually:
- 小象 already produces naive-Bayes probabilities, so Q2 has real input waiting;
- today's bug shows the cost of the hand-rolled two-input Boolean equation parser.

In the meantime, the proposal model can start as plain counts. It moves to a Markov kernel once the report says how.

🈸 (one decision) Shall I count last week's agent ㊭ paragraphs against your replies first, so we see the accepted / declined / no-response numbers before designing anything?

previous_reply_acts.text:
(whether the hook needs to change) It only matters in two cases:
- **Hand edits on the server.** Any push, even of an unrelated branch, rewrites the files in `/home/user-data/www/default`, so any edit made directly there would be lost.
- **HEAD moving.** If HEAD were ever pointed at another branch, the next push would deploy that branch.
